headline_marked: 153-run lead: [[Bangladesh dominate Australia]] in first two days of Darwin Test
headline: 153-run lead: Bangladesh dominate Australia in first two days of Darwin Test
summary: Tanzid Tamim scores the first-ever Test century for Bangladesh in Australia, as the Tigers take a commanding lead after Day 2.
details: Bangladesh have stunned the cricketing world by dominating Australia through the first two days of their opening Test in Darwin, taking a 153-run lead.
Tanzid Tamim made history by becoming the first Bangladeshi player to score a Test century in Australia, striking a superb 101.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto contributed a strong 84, while Hasan Mahmud claimed a career-best 6-55 to bowl Australia out for 198 on Day 1.
The Tigers reached 351-6 at stumps on Day 2, with Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) continuing the lead.
The turnaround is remarkable given Bangladesh's poor preparation, including being bowled out for 54 in a warm-up match and a previous tour in 2003 where they lost both Tests by an innings.
Former Indian off-spinner Ravichandran Ashwin praised the performance, calling it a 'turnaround' and stating that Bangladesh have put Australia on the back foot.
caption:
From 54 all out in a warm-up game to a 153-run lead against Australia. The Tigers are dominating!

Bangladesh have stunned the cricketing world by dominating Australia through the first two days of their opening Test in Darwin, taking a 153-run lead.

Tanzid Tamim made history by becoming the first Bangladeshi player to score a Test century in Australia, striking a superb 101.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto contributed a strong 84, while Hasan Mahmud claimed a career-best 6-55 to bowl Australia out for 198 on Day 1.

The Tigers reached 351-6 at stumps on Day 2, with Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) continuing the lead.

The turnaround is remarkable given Bangladesh's poor preparation, including being bowled out for 54 in a warm-up match and a previous tour in 2003 where they lost both Tests by an innings.

Former Indian off-spinner Ravichandran Ashwin praised the performance, calling it a 'turnaround' and stating that Bangladesh have put Australia on the back foot.

headline: 9 workers die in toxic gas exposure at Sitakunda shipyard
summary: The tragedy occurred at Ferdous Steel, where the Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments had filed a case over safety violations just a month prior.
details: Nine workers died after suspected exposure to toxic gas while cutting scrap inside an old LNG carrier at the Ferdous Steel shipbreaking yard in Sitakunda, Chattogram.
The leak led to a high concentration of carbon monoxide, causing severe breathing difficulties and unconsciousness among the workers.
Five workers died at the scene, while four others passed away during treatment. Another 10 to 12 workers remain hospitalized with serious injuries.
The Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments (DIFE) had filed a case against Ferdous Corporation Ltd on July 15 for failing to implement safety directives.
DIFE officials had issued multiple notices and reminders since February 2 to rectify safety deficiencies, but the shipyard continued operations without adequate measures.
Local labour leaders alleged negligence, stating workers entered the vessel without checks for gas or liquid waste on a day the yard was supposed to be closed.
In the aftermath, two labour inspectors were seriously injured after being assaulted by a mob during a site inspection.
The Department of Environment is investigating whether the shipyard had the necessary permissions from relevant agencies to dismantle the vessel.
caption:
9 workers dead. A shipyard that was already facing legal action for safety violations just one month ago.

Nine workers died after suspected exposure to toxic gas while cutting scrap inside an old LNG carrier at the Ferdous Steel shipbreaking yard in Sitakunda, Chattogram.

The leak led to a high concentration of carbon monoxide, causing severe breathing difficulties and unconsciousness among the workers.

Five workers died at the scene, while four others passed away during treatment. Another 10 to 12 workers remain hospitalized with serious injuries.

The Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments (DIFE) had filed a case against Ferdous Corporation Ltd on July 15 for failing to implement safety directives.

DIFE officials had issued multiple notices and reminders since February 2 to rectify safety deficiencies, but the shipyard continued operations without adequate measures.

Local labour leaders alleged negligence, stating workers entered the vessel without checks for gas or liquid waste on a day the yard was supposed to be closed.

In the aftermath, two labour inspectors were seriously injured after being assaulted by a mob during a site inspection.

The Department of Environment is investigating whether the shipyard had the necessary permissions from relevant agencies to dismantle the vessel.
